newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) rise.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) rise.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Wednesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
The central bank does not post volumes.
Traders said trading was dull, with rates moving in a narrow range and the market under downward pressure on expectations that the central bank would shortly cut bank reserve ratios.
The People's Bank of China, the central bank, has said it will cut the ratios within this year and traders expect the cut to release large amounts of cash into the interbank market.

"On expectations of the bank reserve ratio cut, money supply is sufficient on the market," one trader said. "Financial institutions prefer lending to borrowing before the cut comes into effect, to prevent losses."
